I have been farming in Quzhou for more than twenty years, and I know this land well. The soil is alluvial and fertile, but water and labor are what limit me now. My son works in Handan city and only comes back for the busy harvests, so my wife and I must manage the fields ourselves. That means I cannot take on cotton or vegetables — they need too many pesticide sprays and too much hand labor. The safest, most stable choice is the winter wheat–summer maize double-cropping system that everyone around here grows. The government still gives a subsidy for wheat, the grain station buys at a guaranteed price, and both crops are highly mechanized.

This year I will plant my whole 8 mu to winter wheat. I will buy Luyuan 502, an improved variety that yields reliably in our county. Before sowing I will rotary-till the field to break up the stubble and level the ground. For fertilizer I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and then top-dress urea at the jointing stage — altogether about 25 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times: once before winter to protect the seedlings from freezing, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the spring weather cooperates.

As soon as the wheat comes off the combine in early June, I will plant summer maize without any further tillage — no-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble saves fuel, keeps moisture, and lets me finish sowing in two days before the summer rains start. I will use Denghai 605 hybrid seed; it is what the seed shop always recommends and it performs well here. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat, so I will apply about 20 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu, mostly as a side-dress at the big-trumpet stage. Two irrigations should be enough — one if the early summer is dry, and another at flowering if the rains fail. I will spray herbicide once and then fungicide and insecticide two or three more times as the crop develops. I reckon I can get 550 kg per mu of maize.
